title: BenchmarkClaims
description: Vendor-asserted improvement claim benchmarks for a specific ValueModel. Captures median, minimum, and maximum observed or researched values for each Improvement Claim variable in the referenced model. Published alongside the ValueModel to make vendor assertions transparent, human-checkable, and LLM-usable. Implementations may add fields without breaking conformance.

model_id.description: Identifier of the ValueModel this benchmark data applies to. Should match the identifier used in the value model page front matter.

effective_date.description: ISO date from which these benchmarks are considered current.

claims.description: One entry per Improvement Claim variable in the referenced ValueModel. Every variable with category 'Improvement Claim' should have an entry here.

variable_name.description: References ValueModel.variables[].name for a variable with category 'Improvement Claim'.

display_name.description: Human-readable label for this claim, matching ValueModel.variables[].display_name.

unit.description: The unit in which median, min, and max are expressed. For Percentage variables use '%'. For Money variables use the ISO 4217 currency code. For Numeric variables use a descriptive label (e.g. 'hours', 'days', 'transactions').

median.description: The central or most typical observed value for this improvement claim across the customer base or research corpus.

min.description: The lower bound of the observed or researched range. Represents outcomes for customers with less favourable conditions.

max.description: The upper bound of the observed or researched range. Represents outcomes for customers with the most favourable conditions.

basis.description: The evidentiary basis for this claim. 'customer_data' = measured across actual customers. 'third_party_research' = published external research. 'internal_testing' = controlled internal benchmarks. 'analyst_estimate' = analyst or advisory firm projection. 'vendor_estimate' = vendor's own informed estimate.

notes.description: Optional caveats, scope limitations, or methodology notes for this claim (e.g. 'Based on enterprise segment customers only', 'Measured at 6 months post-implementation').
